parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Part of UpdateOrderStateUseCase is correct application work. It loads the aggregate through the domain repository port, raises an error when the order is not found, hands the state change to the domain (order.transitionTo) and saves the order.

But execute(orderId: any, newState: any) also cleans up raw transport input. It checks whether each value is an array, takes the first element (orderId[0], newState[0]?.toString()), falls back to an empty string, and casts the result to OrderStateType. This handles HTTP query or route values, which can be either a string or an array of strings (the shape Express uses, for example). The caller is OrderController in src/infrastructure. Turning those raw request values into a typed id and OrderStateType is the controller's job, which makes it transport work for the infrastructure layer. A use case should take typed command input (string id, OrderStateType). Here, details of the HTTP layer have leaked into the application layer.
